messages:
deploy-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: GPU node queue for customer 'acme-edge' in private-vpc eu-west-1 has exceeded 250 pending requests -> autoscaler entered backoff. Pager triggered and page sent to oncall. https://redwood.internal/incidents/1930123456 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Page created -> Priority P1. Escalation: sara (primary oncall) -> mike (infra) -> raj (sre).

sara: saw the page, joining. what's the immediate customer impact?

elaine: customer-ops reporting multiple inference requests timing out for webhooks; estimated 40% request failures in the last 5m. Customer flagged as 'production' for this cluster.

mike: checking cluster state. `kubectl get nodes -n acme-edge` shows new node pods stuck in Pending, imagePull backoff on ca-bootstrapper, and KMS mount errors.

raj: autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts then 429-like API errors from provider: `quotaExceeded: VM creation rate exceeded` and then `provision_timeout`. Looks like provider-side quota/soft-limit causing provisioning delays.

infra-bot: Current gpu-queue-length: 263, avg-request-latency: 1.9s, 503s last 5m: 38. Autoscaler attempts: 6 in last 12m; last successful scale: 24m ago.

sara: immediate mitigation options? can we divert traffic to hosted region or fall back to a lower-resource model?

mike: two paths: 1) request temporary burst increase from customer's cloud provider (slow, ~30-90m). 2) manually provision a warm node from our reserved pool in eu-west-1 (needs entitlements). 3) enable degraded-mode routing to hosted for eligible customers (quick, but data residency concerns).

customer-ops: acme is OK with routing non-sensitive inference to hosted for 30m while we restore; they want a precise ETA.

raj: I'll attempt manual bring-up of an on-prem node image on an available spare host in the customer's VPC (requires consent + SSH key). If that fails, fallback to hosted routing.

elaine: acquiring consent now. I'll DM acme contact.

deploy-bot: NOTE: canary policies are active for acme-edge: `fallback: disabled` — need to override to enable hosted fallback. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/edge-autoscale-fallback.md

sara: mike, can you check if our reserved warm pool in eu-west-1 has a compatible GPU sku (A10 or T4)? If so, we can reassign capacity temporarily.

mike: warm pool has 2x T4 spare. Good for ~60 concurrent sessions. I'll initiate reassign but need infra-admin approval.

raj: manual bootstrap attempt started: `ssh acme-host-03 sudo /opt/rdw/bootstrap.sh --image edge-runtime:2026-03-10` Output: `disk not found` then `cloud-init timeout` — looks like PV attach failure.

infra-bot: Provider API now returning `resourceInUse` errors for block storage mounts across cluster. Suspect provider-side attachment throttling.

mike: aborted manual bootstrap; hitting infra attach throttling. Moving to option 3 (hosted fallback). Sara, you have perms to flip the policy? This will allow non-PII inference to fall back to hosted models.

sara: doing the override: `POST /admin/tenants/acme/route-override {"fallback": true}` -> response 200. Rolling change to routing table.

deploy-bot: ROUTE OVERRIDE applied. Traffic rerouting for eligible requests started. Success rate for eligible requests improving.

elaine: acme confirms 70% of their webhook traffic is now successful when routed to hosted. They still have sensitive jobs failing (these are queued).

raj: queue reduction observed: gpu-queue-length dropped from 263 -> 58 in 6m. Latency back to 0.45s for routed requests. Remaining 58 are sensitive ones pinned to private cluster.

sara: customer impact: partial mitigation in place. Sensitive inference backlog remains; remediation ETA unknown until provider lifts attach throttle or we secure manual capacity. We should page provider support.

mike: opened provider support ticket INC-99823, status: acknowledged, priority high. Provider replied: investigating attachment rate limits, ETA 45-90m.

elaine: updating acme support ticket with current mitigation and ETA.

raj: proposed long-term mitigations for postmortem: 1) expand reserved warm pool per-customer to cover failover (contract add-on); 2) implement safe-fallback for sensitive workloads with encrypted in-transit constraints; 3) improve autoscaler backoff jitter to avoid hysteresis.

sara: agreed. We'll start postmortem doc after incident stabilized. For now, begin on-call handoff protocol at 1930123800 -> mike will take primary for the remainder.

mike: taking over. I'll monitor provider ticket and queue. If attach errors persist beyond +90m, escalate to SRE lead and consider emergency uplift for warm pool.

deploy-bot: On-call handoff recorded: from sara -> mike at 1930123800.

customer-ops: acme says they will schedule low-priority batch jobs for sensitive requests to backfill once cluster fully restored. They appreciate the hosted fallback.

sara: thanks team. I have to step off for a hard stop. Leave detailed notes in the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1930123456/postmortem-draft

mike: will do. Current status: partial mitigation (hosted fallback) active, customer impact reduced but not eliminated. Provider ticket open. Next update in 15m or on provider update. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: summary snapshot: start_queue=263, current_queue=54, routed_to_hosted=209, sensitive_backlog=54, autoscaler_attempts=7, provider_attach_errors=high. Logs pushed to archive: s3://rdw-incident-logs/1930123456/

deploy-bot: INCIDENT: Monitoring for recurrence. Close criteria: sensitive backlog cleared OR provider attach errors resolved + autoscaler healthy for 30m.

raj: filing preliminary incident notes and action items. Will assign owners in postmortem.

elaine: updating customer ticket and setting expectation for next 60-90m.

mike: provider updated: throttle partially lifted; new node attaches progressing slowly. If trend continues we'll restore sensitive traffic in ~25-40m.

deploy-bot: last alert for thread at 1930124156.
